source_artifacts.locator: approval queue (as shown to the analyst)

capabilities.target: User's MFA methods; issues a temporary access pass
Chat message to the ticket requester, carrying the temporary access pass

inputs.source: Support ticket, including tickets emailed in by contractors and vendors

instructions.note: The instruction sends the temporary access pass to 'the person who opened the ticket', implicitly treating ticket authorship as proof of account ownership, with no verification step named anywhere in the prompt.

The approval requirement in line 3 is scoped only to the reset action. No approval, identity check, or rate limit is specified for the temporary-pass delivery step, and the ticket source (including external contractor/vendor email) is unbounded.

elements.name: Temporary access pass delivery to ticket requester
Identity provider directory and MFA store

controls.name: Service desk analyst approval in the queue tool
controls.decay_rationale: Enforced by a human analyst outside the model, who reviews the raw target account, requester, and full ticket text before idp.reset_mfa executes (and before the dependent, automatic chat.send_temp_pass fires), so it does not decay with model capability. It fails under autonomy_increase or control_removal (gate narrowed, auto-approval introduced, or removed), and its real-world effectiveness already decays with approval volume (~200 requests/analyst/shift), i.e. approval fatigue (SAFE-T1403).

controls.name: Recipient confirmation bound to the account record (missing)
controls.decay_rationale: Would pull the delivery destination from the account's own verified contact record rather than the ticket's self-reported requester field, so it would not decay with model capability; it would fail only if disabled (control_removal) or if contact/credential scope widens without re-verification (data_scope_expansion).

controls.name: Requester-to-account-owner identity proofing (missing)
controls.decay_rationale: Would require out-of-band proof (step-up auth, manager attestation) that the ticket submitter is the account owner before a reset is queued for approval; enforced outside the model, but would need re-verification if contractor access scope expands (data_scope_expansion).

controls.name: Secondary review or volume cap for external-originated tickets (missing)
controls.decay_rationale: A second reviewer or an enforced per-analyst cap for external-originated resets would reduce approval fatigue, but remains a human judgment control and would still degrade as ticket volume grows (longer_task_horizon) or if waived (control_removal).

findings.title: Confused deputy (SAFE-T1307 / TC4): approved MFA reset delivers the temporary access pass to the unverified ticket requester, not the account owner

attack_path.note: Contractor/vendor can email in a ticket naming any target account and self-declaring as the requester.
Agent looks up the named account.
Agent requests analyst approval and, if approved, removes the account's real MFA factors and issues a temporary pass using a shared service credential.
Agent automatically sends the temporary pass to the ticket requester's address, which is not verified against the account owner.

forecast.watch_signal: Approval gate removed or narrowed (e.g., auto-approval added for tickets matching a 'routine' template), per-request individual review changed to batch or implicit approval, or the queue tool no longer requiring a human click before idp.reset_mfa executes.

evidence.observation: Instruction sends the temporary access pass to 'the person who opened the ticket' rather than the verified account owner.
States contractors and vendors can email tickets in, and the requester field is simply the email sender; the temp pass goes to whoever opened the ticket, not the account owner.

evidence.locator: approval queue (as shown to the analyst)
evidence.observation: The queue entry is scoped to 'Action: idp.reset_mfa' only; there is no separate review step for chat.send_temp_pass, which fires automatically once the reset is approved.

Two analysts approve about 400 requests per shift (~200/analyst/shift), far above the ~20/day threshold this rubric treats as low volume, and most are described as routine, indicating approval-fatigue risk.

recommendations.action: Verify that the ticket requester is the authenticated account owner (e.g., step-up auth on the account's own registered factor, or manager attestation) before the reset request reaches the approval queue, rather than relying on the self-reported 'Requested by' field.
Bind delivery of the temporary access pass to a destination pulled from the account's own verified contact record in the directory, not from the ticket's requester field.

Require a second analyst review, or enforce a per-analyst daily approval cap, for reset requests originating from external (contractor/vendor) email addresses to counter approval fatigue at current volume.
Require the account owner to acknowledge receipt of the temporary pass through an independent, pre-registered channel before it becomes active, so a misdirected pass cannot be used silently.

stride_coverage.rationale: Artifacts do not describe how the agent authenticates to idp.read_user, idp.reset_mfa, or chat.send_temp_pass, so whether the agent's own service identity can be spoofed cannot be assessed.
Artifacts do not describe any protection on the agent's system prompt or runtime configuration against modification, so tampering with the agent itself cannot be assessed.

The approval queue records an approve/reject decision attributable to one of the two service-desk analysts for every idp.reset_mfa request, the only declared attribution mechanism for a sensitive action.

The agent processes one ticket at a time with no described autonomous loop, spend action, or unattended step budget, so runaway resource consumption through this agent is not architecturally possible as described.
This is an inbound flow carrying ticket content into the agent; it does not itself carry data outside the trust boundary, so disclosure is covered instead under el.temp_pass_delivery.
Artifacts do not state whether inbound ticket volume, size, or submission rate from email is validated or rate limited, so flooding risk cannot be assessed.
Artifacts do not describe any verification tying an external submitter's claimed identity to an authenticated record beyond the raw email sender address shown in the queue.

The recipient address for this flow is taken directly from the ticket's requester field, already recorded as a tampering risk on el.ticket_intake; there is no separate in-transit modification point for this outbound flow.
This is a single discrete send per approved reset ticket with no described loop or batching, so denial of service through this flow is not applicable.
Artifacts do not describe access controls protecting queue records from modification after an analyst decision is recorded.
Artifacts do not state who besides the two service-desk analysts can read queue entries, which include full ticket text and target account names.
No capacity failure of the queue tool itself is described; the volume concern here affects decision quality, which is captured in FND-1, not store availability.
Each entry retains an approve/reject decision attributable to one of the two analysts handling the queue.
Artifacts do not state whether idp.read_user is scoped to limit which profile fields or which users' records the agent may query.
No batch or loop capability against the directory is described; actions are one user per approved ticket.

rating.rationale: The only finding (FND-1) chains an untrusted source (support tickets, including contractor/vendor email) through a shared-service-account MFA reset into an irreversible, restricted-sensitivity egress (the temporary pass), which the base matrix rates critical, confirmed by the autonomy modifier since no step or runtime limits are declared. The declared raw-action analyst approval on idp.reset_mfa earns one tier of credit (critical to high) because it is independent of model capability, but it does not sever the path: it covers the reset decision, not a verified binding between the pass's recipient and the account owner, and its real value is further eroded by high approval volume (~200/analyst/shift) and the fact that most requests are routine. Under control_removal or autonomy_increase the gate itself is defeated and the design reverts to its critical inherent tier, so forecast equals critical with ctl.analyst_approval as the control whose decay matters most.

limitations: This assessment reflects the declared design in prompt.md, the approval-queue mock-up, and the runtime notes provided; it does not reflect observed runtime behavior, logs, or live configuration.

No tool manifest, MCP configuration, or IaC was provided, so credential scopes for idp.read_user, idp.reset_mfa, and chat.send_temp_pass are inferred from the described workflow rather than verified; confidence on those scope values is medium to low.

No logging or audit-trail configuration was described beyond the approval queue's own approve/reject record, so repudiation and detection controls for the automated temp-pass send could not be assessed and are recorded as not_assessed rather than mitigated.
